titel: Front of my knee hurts: patellar tendinopathy (trend format, EN)

skript.hook: Patient holds his knee: 'The front of my knee hurts!!!'
skript.aufbau: Physio: 'Where?' → patient points below the kneecap → physio recognises the typical picture: patellar tendinopathy (chef's kiss).
skript.payoff: 4 exercises as a progression: Spanish squat → hip-dominant step-down (easier) → knee-dominant step-down (harder) → single-leg squat to box.

hook.visuell: Schneller Zoom aufs Knie (Hände am Knie) und wieder raus, André gebeugt mit Schmerzgesicht

einblendungen.text:
\*points to the tendon
below the kneecap\*

aussagen.text: Pain at the lower pole of the kneecap (patellar tendon) is the typical key symptom of patellar tendinopathy.
aussagen.quelle: Malliaras P, Cook J, Purdam C, Rio E. Patellar Tendinopathy: Clinical Diagnosis, Load Management, and Advice for Challenging Case Presentations. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 2015;45(11):887–898

aussagen.text: Treatment: progressively increasing tendon load, e.g. isometrics, then slow heavy strength training.
aussagen.quelle: Malliaras P et al. JOSPT 2015;45(11):887–898; Rio E et al. Isometric exercise induces analgesia and reduces inhibition in patellar tendinopathy. Br J Sports Med 2015;49(19):1277–1283

caption:
Pain right below your kneecap, especially on stairs, jumping or squats? That often fits patellar tendinopathy. This is not a remote diagnosis though, get your knee checked.

4 exercises you can try, from easier to harder. Start with the hip-dominant step-down, the knee-dominant one is the harder version.

If something hurts, don't go deeper into the movement.

Save this reel for your next knee workout.
